meta: The voice in this video is read by AI. How does the machine do it? Step 1: turn text into the sounds to make (phonemes). Step 2: work out intonation. Step 3: make the sound wave. Plus: how to spot voice cloning scams.

muc.title: AI reads text out loud
muc.text: Last time, AI turned a voice into text. Now the other way around. The voice in this video is read by AI too. The machine does it in three steps.

muc.title: Text into sounds
muc.text: First, the machine turns text into the sounds it needs to make, called phonemes. The word "knight" has six letters, but only three sounds.

muc.title: Add intonation
muc.text: Then the machine works out the intonation: where the voice goes up, where it pauses, which word gets stressed. "You're home" can be a question or a statement, depending on intonation.

muc.title: Make the sound wave
muc.text: Finally, the model draws a spectrogram like in the last part, then turns it into a sound wave for the speaker. Because it learned from thousands of hours of real people reading, the voice even has breaths and feelings.

muc.title: A few seconds is enough to fake a voice
muc.text: The worrying part: with just a few seconds of a voice sample, AI can copy someone's voice. Scammers can take your voice from videos you post, then call your family asking for money fast.

muc.title: Strange calls asking for money
muc.text: Remember the earlier video about fake faces? Now voices can be faked too. When a family member calls asking for money urgently, hang up and call back on the number you know.

muc.title: Listen to an article, set a family password
muc.text: Today, turn on read-aloud to listen to a long article while you wash the dishes. Then set a family password with everyone at home, to ask for when a strange call asks for money.

muc.title: Listening and talking together
muc.text: What happens when listening and talking come together? We chat with AI like with a real person. See you in part 3.
